body:
lmwindham@bluebon.net wrote, in response to the population problem, and
suggested revisitng paragraphs 204 and 205 of the manifesto (which urged
revolutionaries to have as many children as they could, despite their concerns
about overpopulation, which led them to having "few or no children"):

"One of the many moments in which K's psyche gets the better of him, and one of
the many moments in which he and I part company."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
----------------

Lmwindham, I don't get your point.
Perhaps you should revisit paragraphs 189: "...revolutionaries should not
expect to have a majority of people on their side..." and 187: "On the more
sophisticated level the ideology should address itself to people who are
intelligent, thoughtful and rational. The object should be to create a core of
people who will be opposed to the industrial system on a rational, thought-out
basis, with full appreciation of the problems and ambiguites involved, and of
the price that has to be paid for getting rid of the system. It is particularly
important to attract people of this type, as they are capable people and will
be instrumental in influencing others."

Paragraph 205 makes perfect sense in this context.

The more thoughtful people, the merrier!
Esjeje1@aol.com
"Whoso wants to be a man must also be a non-conformist" - Emerson
